about: Opt-in mods for long-context MoE decode and prefill. Series order = list order. Every gain is against this engine's stock code path (the unpatched build, or the same build with the switch off). archived: rejected patches, kept so nothing is lost; never in the series (archive/README.md is generated from the rows).

gain.conditions: RTX 5090, one request at a time, 59-turn session to 128k context, MoE model on the engine's qwen4exp graph (hybrid indexer, k-pool 4, top-k 2048), q8_0 KV, MTP draft head k=3, -ncmoe 16 --moe-cache-mib 6400, series switches 01-08 on, -ub 128 -b 2048; 2 alternating pairs + off-vs-off (-2.9 ms); decode tok/s unchanged (+0.00% [-0.15, +0.16])

limits: batches over 32 tokens through the MMQ mul_mat_id kernel only; decode and small batches keep the stock path
experts that miss the cache are still uploaded one by one into the staging copy, as stock (about 116 ms a turn at 100k remains)
one device-side offset table per staged host expert tensor (2 KB each, kept for the life of the backend context)
a cold first turn is unchanged (nothing is cached yet)

static.note: 10 hunks rewrite stock lines: the MMQ kernel and its launch take one more argument (x_delta), and its three tile call sites read x + x_delta[zt] when x_delta is set; with the switch unset x_delta is nullptr and the weight base is x, as stock. The MoE cache callback computes the offsets only with the switch on.

mods.exercised_by: llama-server context checkpoints (three a prompt) on a CUDA device with a pinned host buffer type; any model whose state saves are 1 MiB or more
limits: costs 3.7 GB of pinned host RAM (33 x 113 MiB here: --ctx-checkpoints + 1 buffers of the state size) from the first checkpoint until the process exits
the first checkpoint of a server's life takes about 2.3 s once (all pool buffers are pinned at once)
costs 8 MiB of VRAM (measured stacked on 10 at -ub 512)

a checkpoint of another size or past the reserved count is pinned when first needed (slower host CUDA calls while that happens); buffers under 1 MiB and hosts without a pinned host buffer type take the stock path
the check mode doubles checkpoint memory

static.note: purely additive (0 lines removed): the pool is behind the state buffer allocator and is never entered with the switch unset; 65 of the 70 server lines are the check mode.

archived.name: kv-host-old
archived.written_on: 1.0.0 + 01 + 02 (applies there; the two tested trees hold it after the whole series)
archived.why: KV cells older than a window in mapped host memory. Bit-identical, frees about 1.05-1.4 GiB, but costs +14.6 ms/step at 96-128k for about 4 ms of expert layers bought back. Rejected by its own cutoff rule at every window. Its code is still in both tested trees (switch unset in every kept measurement): tested_trees apply this archived copy, pinned by sha256, only to reach byte equality.

archived.name: kv-staged-gather-a2
archived.why: staged gather of a call's union of old rows (derived 0.65-0.79 ms/step fetch). Designed, never compiled, never measured. Depends on kv-host-old. The patch was written (switch LLAMA_KV_STAGE, check LLAMA_KV_STAGE_CHECK=N) but its build log is empty: never compiled, never measured. Rejected with kv-host-old, which it needs.

archived.name: sparse-direct-half2
archived.written_on: the run's working tree (01 + an earlier cut of 02's half 1, base committed as 678b0933 in the run's src/); it does not apply on 1.0.0 + 01 + 02
archived.why: Half 2 of sparse-direct: index lists straight from top-k, no mask scan (under 02's switch LLAMA_SPARSE_DIRECT, so no switch of its own). Bit-exact once the lists were ordered, but -1.0% [-1.3, -0.6] on the 128k session against half 1 alone (worse under 96k, zero at 96-128k), and it frees nothing because the n_kv mask is still built. Dropped before 02 was cut.
